Follow-up bounded task (same honesty/evidence rules; scratch in your agents/<actor_id>/ area, deliverable notes only — no changes to my mech/, src/, results/).

Context: I am reducing USC Mech II (Wang/You/Joshi/Davis/Laskin/Egolfopoulos/Law 2007, "USC Mech Version II", 111 species/784 reactions, high-T C1–C4) via graph-based skeletal reduction, validated on ignition delay + laminar flame speed. For the final report I need a compact, factual LITERATURE CONTEXT note. Please research and write agents/<actor_id>/lit_context.md (then team_submit a reference to it) covering:

1. USC-II's own stated scope/validation: fuels, observables, T/P/phi ranges in the original 2007 paper and/or its accompanying materials (find a public abstract/preprint/author copy; record exact URL and what it actually says — do not rely on memory or secondary summaries alone).
2. Published reductions of USC-II specifically, if any (search e.g. "USC Mech II reduced", "USC-II skeletal", "reduced USC Mech"): report mechanism sizes (species/reactions), reduction method, validation observables/errors claimed, and exact source (URL/DOI, e.g. journal pages, conference papers, theses, GitHub). If none found, say so explicitly with the queries tried.
3. Two or three well-known small C1–C4 mechanisms used as reference points in the community (e.g. San Diego Mechanism, FFCM-2, GRI-Mech 3.0, Aramco small): species/reaction counts and their stated application domains, with URLs. These will serve as context for our accuracy/complexity trade-off.

Keep it to facts you can back with a URL you actually retrieved; label anything you could not verify as unverified. Max ~2 pages. This is literature discovery only — no simulations.

**1. USC-II stated scope**: original `ignis.usc.edu` site is defunct (HTTP 400/TLS failure; archive.org/archive.ph/r.jina.ai all unreachable from this environment). Verbatim page text survives in public mirror `jiweiqi/CollectionOfMechanisms` — quoted: 111 species/784 reactions, high-T oxidation of H2, CO, C1–C4 hydrocarbons, full lineage and the validation claim "against reliable H2/CO/C1-C4 combustion data". Specific T/P/phi validation ranges are **not** in the retrieved text — explicitly labeled *unverified*, not quoted from memory. Local `parent.yaml` confirmed 111/784.

**2. Published USC-II reductions** (4 peer-reviewed, abstracts retrieved via OpenAlex):
- Lytras/Koutmos/Dogkas 2019 — DRG 111→31 sp (then 22, quasi-global 14), turbulent CH4; DOI 10.1134/s0010508219020023
- Lin et al. 2020 (STGSA) — USC-II→33 sp ethylene, accurate IDT+Su; DOI 10.1016/j.combustflame.2020.12.004
- Liu et al. 2018 (GT2018-76855) — GPS+GA→13 sp sCO2 oxy-combustion, P 150–300 atm, T 900–1800 K, phi 0.7–1.3, <12% autoignition error
- Wu/Lin/Law/Yang 2024 (STLSA), DOI 10.1002/kin.21721; plus a 2026 Zenodo preprint
- Takeaway: all are application-specific; no general-purpose reduced USC-II exists.

**3. Reference mechanisms** (counts verified by parsing distributed files): GRI-Mech 3.0 = 53 sp/325 rxn (Cantera `gri30.yaml`; natural-gas domain per OSTI GRI-Mech 1.2 report); FFCM-1 = 38/291 (Stanford `mech-FFCM1.cti`; C0–C2, T>1000 K); FFCM-2 = 96/1054 (`FFCM2_model.yaml`; C0–C4, 1192 targets). San Diego Mechanism: official hosts dead (DNS ENOTFOUND / HTTP 000) — listed but counts explicitly marked unverified.
